title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning — queueing, fairness, starvation prevention, timeouts
author: Asha Patel
description: Tune continuous-batcher scheduler to improve queueing fairness, reduce starvation of small/long-running requests, and tighten timeouts. Motivation: customers observed long-tail latency regressions under mixed workloads (short chat messages + long completion jobs). This PR adjusts aging-based priority, introduces per-request queue-time limits, refactors scheduling loop to reduce wakeups, and adds observability and tests. Changes are backwards-compatible configuration knobs (defaults tuned), include benchmark results showing 95th/99th tail latency reduction for small requests with <1% throughput regression, and update docs and config. Checklist: - [x] Scheduler logic changes implemented - [x] Config knobs exposed and documented - [x] Unit + integration tests added - [x] Benchmarks and perf notes included - [x] Metrics/tracing added - [x] QA on staging (canary) passed

release_notes: continuous-batcher: improved fairness under mixed workloads (reduces starvation of small requests)
Added new scheduler knobs: max_queue_time_ms, aging_weight, priority_buckets
Default timeouts tightened to reduce tail latency for short-lived requests
Backwards-compatible config; previous behavior preserved when knobs set to legacy values
benchmarks_summary: Staging perf canary: mixed workload (80% short chat, 20% long completions) shows p95 latency for short requests decreased from 210ms -> 145ms and p99 from 480ms -> 320ms. Aggregate throughput dropped by ~0.7%. Starvation_count metric dropped to ~0 over 1h steady-state. Detailed scripts added under scripts/perf.
notes: Configuration defaults chosen conservatively after multiple runs across GPU families (A100/V100/RTX). Customers can tune aging_weight and max_queue_time_ms per tenant to prioritize latency vs throughput. Operator docs updated with recommended presets for Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
incident_related: Not an incident hotfix; motivated by customer-reported tail latency in SUP-4123. Verified no regressions in recent incident playbooks.
